items.title: Carbon Emission & Energy Forecasting
items.tagline: Predicting a data center's next move, one timestep at a time.
items.description: A time-series forecasting pipeline for data center energy prediction, built around a Bidirectional LSTM (DRNN) to learn temporal dependencies, with hyperparameter tuning via the Ninja Optimization Algorithm (NiOA).
highlights: Designed multi-horizon forecasting: ΔEk(t) = E(t + k) − E(t)
Enforced strict time-series integrity to avoid data leakage across horizons
Applied NiOA for hyperparameter tuning instead of manual grid search
items.challenge: Multi-horizon forecasting made it easy to accidentally leak future information into training — the pipeline had to be restructured to guarantee strict temporal ordering.
items.lesson: Optimization algorithms borrowed from other fields (like NiOA) can outperform textbook tuning approaches when the search space is large and non-convex.

items.title: Jenkins Job Template Engine
items.description: A template-based CI automation system that generates Jenkins jobs on demand using Python and Jinja2, with job creation automated through the Jenkins REST API.
highlights: Designed a YAML-driven, reusable pipeline templating system
Automated Jenkins job creation end-to-end through the REST API
Developed multi-stage, parameterized CI workflows from a single template source
items.challenge: Keeping pipeline templates generic enough to reuse across projects while still allowing per-job parameters without duplicating YAML.
items.lesson: A small, well-designed templating layer removes far more manual Jenkins configuration than expected.

items.title: Data Drift Prediction in ML Systems
items.tagline: Catching a model's accuracy before it quietly slips.
items.description: A proactive system that predicts data drift and forecasts model accuracy degradation based solely on input distribution shifts, without needing ground-truth labels.
highlights: Used the CICIDS 2017 dataset to realistically simulate distribution shift
Built a modular pipeline architecture for easy integration into existing ML systems
Predicted accuracy degradation from input distribution alone, ahead of ground truth
items.challenge: Detecting meaningful drift (versus normal data noise) without access to labels required careful choice of distributional distance metrics.
items.lesson: Monitoring input distributions is a surprisingly effective early-warning system for silent model decay.
